short: The auto-drafted statement of the input tax credit available to you.
seoTitle: GSTR-2B — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: The auto-drafted statement of the input tax credit available to you. It is the reference point for how much credit can legitimately be claimed.
definition: GSTR-2B is a static, auto-drafted statement generated for each tax period listing the input tax credit available to a business based on what its suppliers have reported. It is the reference point for how much credit can legitimately be claimed.
bodyHtml:
Why GSTR-2B matters

Credit claimed beyond what GSTR-2B shows is the single most common mismatch in GST scrutiny. Reconciling against it turns supplier non-compliance into something you can chase in the same month rather than discover a year later.

How GSTR-2B works in practice

Match your purchase register line by line against GSTR-2B, and keep a short list of suppliers whose invoices repeatedly fail to appear. That list is usually a better negotiating tool than any reminder email.

faq.question: What is the difference between GSTR-2A and GSTR-2B?
faq.answer: GSTR-2A is dynamic and keeps updating as suppliers file, while GSTR-2B is a static snapshot for the period.

faq.question: Can I claim credit that is missing from GSTR-2B?
faq.answer: Not reliably. Until the supplier reports the invoice, the credit is not considered available.
